title: Remainder when a cubic with a missing square term is divided by x-c
source: P23 Ch1 theory P23-1.4 Quick check 1 (2x^3+x-5 divided by x-1, remainder -2)
stem: Find the remainder when the cubic with coefficients {a|int} (of \(x^3\)), 0 (of \(x^2\)), {b|int} (of \(x\)) and constant term {d|int} is divided by \(x-c\), where \(c={c|int}\).

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: Write the dividend as \({a|int}x^3+0x^2+{b|int}x+{d|int}\) and divide by \(x-{c|int}\) until a constant remainder remains. (The remainder is the value of the dividend at \(x={c|int}\), but the method of this subsection is the division itself.)
steps.note: Set out the long division, including a 0x^2 placeholder.

contexts.stem: Using algebraic long division, find the remainder when \({a|int}x^3+{b|int}x+{d|int}\) is divided by \(x-c\), where \(c={c|int}\).
The cubic \({a|int}x^3+{b|int}x+{d|int}\) has no square term. Find the remainder when it is divided by \(x-c\), where \(c={c|int}\).

title: Leading coefficient of the quotient of a cubic divided by a linear polynomial
source: P23 Ch1 theory P23-1.4 Quick check 2 (6x^3 divided by 2x+1, leading coefficient 3)
stem: The cubic \({A|int}x^3-x^2+x+4\) is divided by \({s|int}x+1\). What is the leading coefficient of the quotient?

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: The first term of the quotient is \({A|int}x^3\div {s|int}x={q|int}x^2\).

steps.name: E
steps.text_tex: The leading coefficient of the quotient is \({E|int}\).

contexts.stem: In the long division of \({A|int}x^3-x^2+x+4\) by \({s|int}x+1\), what is the leading coefficient of the quotient?
A cubic beginning \({A|int}x^3\) is divided by a linear factor beginning \({s|int}x\). Write down the leading coefficient of the quotient.

title: Quotient and remainder when 2x^3+3x^2+10 is divided by (x+2)

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF. Steps and marks from the official MS PDF. Independently: writing 2x^3+3x^2+0x+10 and dividing by (x+2) gives quotient 2x^2-x+2 and remainder 6, because (x+2)(2x^2-x+2)+6=2x^3+3x^2+10. Fully manual, because the official part asks for a quotient and a remainder. The official special case awarding B1 only for using the remainder theorem to give 6 is noted, but the method of this subsection is algebraic division.

stem: Find the quotient and the remainder when \(2x^3+3x^2+10\) is divided by \((x+2)\).

steps.name: div
steps.text_tex: Write the dividend as \(2x^3+3x^2+0x+10\) and divide by \(x+2\). The first two terms of the quotient have the form \(2x^2+kx\).
steps.note: MS: M1 Divide and obtain a quotient as far as 2x^2+kx.

steps.name: r
steps.note: MS: A1 Obtain remainder 6. Special case: use of the remainder theorem to give 6 is B1 only.

title: Quotient when p(x)=4x^3+16x^2+9x-15 is divided by (2x+3), remainder -6

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF for part (a) only. Later parts of Q6 (integration and a trigonometric equation) are omitted because they lie outside this subsection. Independently: (2x+3)(2x^2+5x-3)-6=4x^3+16x^2+9x-15. Fully manual. Note that 9709/22/F/M/22 Q2 was used in P23-1.2; this is a different question from the same paper.

stem:
The polynomial \(p(x)\) is given by \(p(x)=4x^3+16x^2+9x-15\).
(a) Find the quotient when \(p(x)\) is divided by \((2x+3)\), and show that the remainder is \(-6\).

steps.name: div
steps.text_tex: Divide \(4x^3+16x^2+9x-15\) by \(2x+3\), obtaining a quotient that begins \(2x^2+kx\).
steps.note: MS: M1 Divide and obtain a quotient as far as 2x^2+kx.

steps.name: r
steps.text_tex: The remainder is \(-6\), as required. (The official scheme requires enough detail to confirm the given remainder.)
steps.note: MS: A1 Confirm remainder is -6. AG — necessary detail needed.
